correctness.rationale: Direct independent SymPy differentiation of the explicit polynomial L=(z^2+(1-y)^2)/2+(x^2-1)(1-y) yields Ldot=2 x^2(1-y)^2-a z^2. For a<0, nonnegative Ldot=0 requires z=0 and x(1-y)=0; imposing invariance leaves exactly E0,Eplus,Eminus. For a=0, its largest invariant zero set is x=0 with harmonic y,z oscillator plus Eplus/Eminus. Forward boundedness ensures global continuation and a compact connected invariant omega-limit set on which L is constant; connectedness and zero-set dynamics leave either an equilibrium or the plane. Off the plane x(t) retains its sign. If its omega-limit lay in the plane, x(t)->0; integrating zdot=x^2-y and bounded z gives Cesaro mean y->0, contradicting (log|x(T)|-log|x(0)|)/T->1 and boundedness. Invariant compactly supported probabilities integrate nonnegative Ldot to zero and disintegrate into uniform angular measures on periodic harmonic orbits. All claims are conditional on forward boundedness; no false global bound on all initial states is needed.
risk: Proof classifies forward-bounded trajectories, not all orbits; some may be unbounded or have finite forward existence.
Invariant measure classification does not classify every compact invariant set, which could contain nonrecurrent connecting orbits.

value.rationale: This exact flow is an established model for reflection-symmetric chaotic behavior at positive parameter values, so proving the sharp complementary nonpositive damping bounded-recurrence regime is a natural dynamical boundary. The explicit globally polynomial Lyapunov identity, forced convergence on open half-spaces, harmonic critical plane, and complete stationary-measure characterization are mutually reinforcing structural results, not a numerical sweep.
risk: The theorem does not assert global boundedness, general compact invariant set classification, or dynamics for a>0.

final_claim: For the reflection-symmetric quadratic flow xdot=x(1-y), ydot=z, zdot=-y-a z+x^2 at every a<=0, every forward-bounded off-plane solution converges to its same-sign nonzero equilibrium; on the symmetry plane a<0 only the origin is forward bounded and a=0 all trajectories are harmonic circles. The compactly supported invariant probabilities are precisely mixtures of those equilibria and, at a=0, uniform measures on the harmonic circles.
limitations: Forward-boundedness is essential: not every initial condition is known globally bounded.
Compactly supported invariant probability measures need not exhaust nonrecurrent compact invariant sets.
No claims for a>0 or other nonlinear jerk flows.
